correctness.rationale: Convergent geometric expansion into nonnegative rank-one kernels; any finite Gram null vector kills two complete moment sequences. A complex Vandermonde inverse recovers two grouped moments per distinct projection; every spherical projection fiber has at most two heights and is then inverted. Harmonic degree and azimuthal order of both feature ladders give exact spectral occupancy. Real-part strictness follows from positive real quadratic forms; the zonal density 3v²-1 annihilates every feature and proves nonuniversality. No infinite assertion rests on the finite checker.

value.rationale: Exact constructive boundary in spherical covariance/interpolation theory: arbitrarily many sites have nonsingular kernel matrices even though the active Laplace eigenspace fraction decays as 2/(2l+1), and a real-valued covariance has only four active high-degree modes. The explicit non-universal witness demonstrates a genuine separation between finite-site interpolation and uniform approximation. This substantially improves interpretability of sparse nonisotropic positive-definiteness compared with sufficient criteria requiring nearly complete harmonic support; it is not a routine scalar substitution or a finite enumeration.
